tldr: The thread opened Oct 21-22 with production write-ups (AWS Deep Insight, DoorDash flag cleanup) and a paper on herding cascades in multi-agent LLM systems, followed by a run of arXiv benchmarks and training, memory and orchestration methods for long-horizon agents. From Nov 1 the focus turned to the evals themselves: task depth, non-English tool use, LLM-judge drift and single-run variance.
whats_new: Two Nov 9 benchmarks put agents on operator work: Infrathon tests long-horizon AI infrastructure optimization, and WorkflowArena scores multi-agent systems on producing executable workflow orchestrations.
why_it_matters: Multi-agent and long-horizon agent results are only as useful as the eval behind them, and the newest benchmarks now target infra tuning and workflow orchestration, the work platform teams would actually hand an agent.

status.detail: A broad research cluster on multi-agent and long-horizon agents, now converging on benchmarks for infrastructure and orchestration work and on whether existing evals measure what they claim.

beats.headline: Multi-agent systems meet production: write-ups and failure modes
beats.summary: Industry case studies sit next to a paper showing agents herding into runaway cascades.

beats.headline: Long-horizon agents get exam-style benchmarks
beats.summary: Continual learning, long web search, robot control and SAST-versus-agent security coverage get their own evals.

Memory, harnesses and learned orchestration for agent teams
beats.summary: Papers on self-evolving teams, memory governance, harness design and runtime-checked orchestration.

beats.headline: Loosely linked: quantization, retrieval and other side papers
beats.summary: These items share vocabulary with the thread but are not about evaluating agents; only the KV-cache paper targets multi-agent serving.

beats.headline: The evals themselves come under scrutiny
beats.summary: Depth, language coverage, judge drift and run-to-run variance all challenge what a single score means.

beats.headline: Benchmarks target infra tuning and workflow orchestration

open_questions: Will other benchmark authors adopt a depth measure beyond turns needed to pass a task?
Will multi-run Monte Carlo reporting become standard in agent benchmark releases?
Do results on τ-bench-LILT show a measurable gap between English and other languages for tool-using agents?
How do frontier agents score on Infrathon's infrastructure optimization tasks compared with human baselines?
Does WorkflowArena show multi-agent orchestration beating a single agent on the same tasks?
take_for_builders: Before giving an agent infra or orchestration work, run the task several times and report the spread, and recheck any LLM judge in your eval against fresh human labels.
